table.caption: Spring frog counts in a restored wetland (invented data for practice)

items.q: A town’s water use rose from 4,000 to 5,000 liters per day. Write the setup for the percent change, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Divide by the old (starting) value, 4,000, not the new one.
Multiply by 100 to turn the fraction into a percent.
20% is the change divided by the new value. Divide by the old value, 4,000.
0.25 is the fraction. Multiply by 100: 25%.

items.q: A forest of 800 hectares lost 120 hectares to logging. By what percent did the forest area change?

mistakes.why: You divided by the new area (680). Percent change divides by the starting area, 800.
Multiply the fraction by 100 for a percent.

items.q: Coal provides 18% of a country’s 4.0 million GWh of electricity. How many GWh is that?

mistakes.why: You multiplied by 18, not 18%. Divide the percent by 100 first: 0.18 × 4,000,000.
You dropped "million". 18% of 4.0 million is 0.72 million = 720,000 GWh.

items.q: Of 2,500 kg of household waste, 650 kg was recycled. What percent was recycled?

mistakes.why: 0.26 is the fraction. Multiply by 100 for a percent.
You divided 2,500 by 650. The part (650) goes on top.

items.q: Which setup gives the percent change from 80 to 60?

why.correct: New minus old, in brackets, divided by the old value, times 100: $-25\%$.
options: Right: brackets, old value on the bottom, × 100.
Without brackets the division happens first, so it is not the change.
That divides by the new value and reverses the sign.
That divides by the new value.

items.q: Better insulation and new appliances cut a home’s electricity use from 9,600 kWh to 6,000 kWh a year. What is the percent decrease? Give a positive number.

mistakes.why: You divided by the new value (6,000). Use the starting value, 9,600.
3,600 kWh is the change itself. Divide by 9,600 and multiply by 100.

items.q: A fish population fell 50% one year and rose 50% the next. Compared with the start, the population is...
options: 25% lower
the same
25% higher
50% lower

why.correct: Start 100 → $100 \times 0.5 = 50$ → $50 \times 1.5 = 75$, which is 25% below 100. Each percent is of a different starting value.
options: Right: 75 is 25% below 100.
The 50% rise is of a smaller number, so it does not undo the fall.
It ends below the start.
It recovered part of the loss.

items.q: Write the setup for the percent change in frogs from 2020 to 2022, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Put brackets around 150 - 120. Without them the division happens first.
Divide by the 2020 value (120), the starting value.
30 is the change in frogs. Divide by 120 and multiply by 100 for a percent.

items.q: What was the percent change in frogs from 2022 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You divided by 135. Percent change divides by the earlier value, 150 (and the change is a decrease).
The size is right, but frogs went down: the percent change is negative, -10%.

items.q: What was the percent change in frogs over the whole period, from 2020 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You added +25% and -10%. Percents of different starting values do not add; use the 2020 and 2024 counts.
You divided by 135. Divide by the 2020 count, 120.

items.q: Which statement describes the frog counts?
options: They rose 25%, then fell 10%, ending 12.5% above 2020.
They rose 25% and kept rising.
They fell over the whole period.
They rose 15% overall, since 25 - 10 = 15.
Right: each change computed from its own start.
The count fell from 2022 to 2024.
135 is above 120.
Percent changes from different starting values do not simply add.

items.q: A wetland covers 2,000 hectares. Development removes 15% of it. How many hectares of wetland are left?

mistakes.why: 300 ha is the area removed (15% of 2,000). The question asks what is left: 2,000 - 300.
You subtracted 15, not 15%. First find 15% of 2,000 ha (300 ha), then subtract.

why.correct: Area removed: (15 / 100) × 2,000 ha = 300 ha. Area left: 2,000 ha - 300 ha = 1,700 ha.

items.q: A fishery’s yearly catch fell from 500 to 400 metric tons. One student reports a 20% decrease and another reports a 25% decrease. Who is right?
options: The second: the change of 100 is divided by the new value, 400
The first: the change of 100 is divided by the old value, 500
Both: either value can go on the bottom
Neither: the decrease is 100%, because the change is 100

why.correct: (400 - 500) / 500 × 100 = -20%, a 20% decrease. Percent change always divides by the old value, the starting point.
options: Dividing by the new value gives 25%, which compares the change with the wrong starting point.
Right: the catch started at 500, so 500 goes on the bottom.
The two choices give different answers, and only the old value is the starting point.
100 metric tons is the change itself. A percent compares it with the starting 500.

items.q: A home used 4,000 liters of water in a month, and 1,400 liters of it went to watering the garden. Write the setup for the percent of the water that went to the garden, then give the answer.

why.correct: $\frac{1{,}400}{4{,}000} \times 100 = 35\%$. The part goes on top, the whole on the bottom, and × 100 makes it a percent.

mistakes.why: The part (the garden, 1,400) goes on top and the whole (4,000) on the bottom.
Multiply by 100 to turn the fraction into a percent.
0.35 is the fraction. Multiply by 100: 35%.
You divided the whole by the part. The garden is the part: 1,400 / 4,000 × 100.

items.q: A region generates 800 GWh of electricity a year: 35% from coal, 40% from natural gas and the rest from other sources. How many GWh come from the other sources?

mistakes.why: 600 GWh is the coal and natural gas together (75%). The other sources are the rest: 100% - 75% = 25%.
25 is the percent from other sources. Take 25% of 800 GWh.

why.correct: Share from other sources: 100% - (35% + 40%) = 25%. Then (25 / 100) × 800 GWh = 200 GWh.

items.q: Town A’s water use rose from 200 to 300 million liters a year. Town B’s rose from 2,000 to 2,500 million liters a year. Which statement is correct?
options: Town B had the larger percent increase, because its use rose by more liters
Both towns had the same percent increase
Town A had the larger increase in liters and in percent
Town A had the larger percent increase, though Town B’s use rose by more liters

why.correct: Town A: (300 - 200) / 200 × 100 = 50%. Town B: (2,500 - 2,000) / 2,000 × 100 = 25%. Town B added more liters (500 million against 100 million), but Town A’s change is larger compared with where it started.
options: A bigger change in liters is not a bigger percent change. Town B’s 500 is compared with a much larger starting value.
The percent increases are 50% and 25%.
Town A’s use rose by 100 million liters, less than Town B’s 500 million.
Right: percent change compares each change with its own starting value.
